title: First time on the road: total commitment to music
summary: In 1951 Monk faced fear of leaving, giving up the trucks and houses, and committing completely to music.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Was this the first time you had even been on the road?
Yeah, it was really the first, ever...
...to give serious thoughts about it even, you know.
What was, just about, that was one of the big periods of the band's popularity...
It sure was. That was the band. He'll say that, and it's pretty well known, that that particular period, that band, that time...

And when I went out to join that band, like I said, I'd never been on a plane and I was trying to prepare myself for it. No fears. I was loaded with them but I had to prepare myself for them. I was trying to prepare myself to walk away from what that was, that I had to cut myself loose, and that wasn't easy to do either. But I had to adjust, I had to make that move.
It was a period in my life, it was like all the thoughts and dreams of the trucks and the houses and the overtime and all that kind of stuff just fizzled. It just wasn't there. It

was like, now I want to be really a professional and dedicated musician. See, it was my life. Music was my life. It was really, really my life. And I'm the type of person by nature, when I make a commitment, it's a total commitment. And I don't compromise. 'Til today, it's the same way. So this... even when I was back selling ice and coal, that was it, I didn't compromise. That was it, when I made that mind to do it, I did that. When I came to Indianapolis and made that total commitment, that was it. No compromising.
And when I made that step, it was really a giant step. I had to get rid of all my fears, at least put them behind me. I wasn't...they were there, but at least they weren't in front of me.
